method.automated: axe-core rules tagged wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa, run on every Storybook story in light and dark, and on open popups (menus, listboxes, dialogs), on every pull request; a new violation fails the build.
method.contrast: Every colour role pair is tested for 4.5:1 (text) and 3:1 (non-text) at standard, medium and high contrast in light and dark.
method.manual: Keyboard behaviour and screen-reader output are documented per component, with step-by-step VoiceOver and NVDA scripts for the complex ones (/foundations/accessibility#screen-reader-scripts); recorded sessions are not published yet.

components.name: Approval Card
screenReader: The outcome ("Approved", "Approved with changes", "Denied") and "Working…" are announced in a polite live region; the card is a group named by its title.
Edit moves focus to the arguments field; Cancel returns it to Edit. Once the choice resolves, focus moves to the card, so it is never lost with the buttons.

components.name: Aurora
screenReader: Decorative: the whole layer is `aria-hidden`.

components.name: Avatar
screenReader: Avatar reads its `name`, plus the `status` ("Ada Lovelace, Away"). Without a name it is decorative and hidden.
AgentAvatar is always `role="img"` and its name says it is an AI agent ("Payhub agent, AI agent", from `messages.aiAgent`). The glyph and the sparkle are hidden.

components.name: Badge
keyboard: —: Badges are non-interactive and have no keyboard handlers.
screenReader: Reads as inline text. For live status changes, wrap in an element with `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"`.
Skipped in tab order. Decorative — never trap focus on a Badge.

components.name: Bar Chart
screenReader: The chart is a `figure` named by `title`. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table carries every value.
Colour is never the only cue: the legend and table name each series. Past six series, label directly or group the rest as "Other".

12.3: the change callout is visible text and describes the figure (`aria-describedby`). Annotations and reference lines are drawn and also listed in a visually hidden "Chart notes" list that describes the figure too.

12.3: the product accent stays out of charts, notes included: guides and labels use the outline and on-surface tokens, and only the change callout and a reference line `tone` take success or error, where the colour means good or bad.

components.name: Button
keyboard: Space: Activates the focused button.
Enter: Activates the focused button.
Tab: Moves focus to the button in document order.
screenReader: Announces the visible label plus the implicit "button" role.
While loading the button sets `aria-busy` and `aria-disabled` (not `disabled`), so focus stays on it and clicks are ignored.
A button with `status` or `loading` renders a polite `role="status"` region next to it that announces `loadingLabel`, `successLabel` or `errorLabel` as the status changes.
Receives focus in document order; `disabled` removes it from the tab sequence.
Visible focus ring uses `--color-border-focus` and meets WCAG 2.4.7 contrast.

components.name: Card
keyboard: Tab: Focuses interactive children. The card itself is never focusable; with a CardLink, the link is.
screenReader: Group related content with a heading inside the Card so AT users can navigate by heading level.
With a CardLink inside, the focus ring is drawn on the card, not around the title.
Prefer CardLink over wrapping the whole card in `<a>`: the link’s accessible name stays the title instead of every word on the card.

components.name: Celebrate
screenReader: Decorative (`aria-hidden`). Announce the win in text, for example in a Toast or a status message.

components.name: Chart Toggle
keyboard: Tab / Space: Move between series and switch one on or off.
screenReader: Each series is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`. The last visible series cannot be switched off.

components.name: Chart Zoom
keyboard: Arrow keys / Home / End: Move the focused thumb.

components.name: Checkbox Card
keyboard: Tab: Moves focus to the card.
Space: Toggles the card.
screenReader: The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description.
Wrap related cards in a `fieldset` with a `legend` so the set has a name.

components.name: Citation
keyboard: Tab: Focuses a marker and opens its preview.
Enter: Opens the source in a new tab.
screenReader: Markers are named "Source 1: <title>", not just the number.
The hover preview repeats the marker’s information; nothing in it is only available on hover.

components.name: Color Picker
keyboard: Enter / Space: Opens the popover with focus on the picked swatch.
Arrow keys: Move between swatches and pick (six per row).
Home / End: First and last swatch.
Tab: Moves to the hex field. Enter or leaving it applies the hex.
Escape: Closes the popover.

components.name: Combobox Field
keyboard: Enter / Space / Arrow Down: Opens the list with focus in the search box.
Arrow Up / Arrow Down: Moves through the options.
Enter: Picks the highlighted option and closes.
Escape: Closes without changing the value.

components.name: Command List
keyboard: Arrow Up / Arrow Down: Moves the highlight; wraps at the ends.
Home / End: Moves to the first or last item.
Enter: Picks the highlighted item.

components.name: Command Palette
keyboard: Cmd/Ctrl + shortcut: Toggles the palette when `shortcut` is set.
Arrow Up / Down: Moves through items (wraps).
Enter: Runs the highlighted item.
Backspace: On an empty query, goes back a page.
Escape: Closes the palette.
screenReader: Focus moves to the input on open and returns to the previously focused element on close.

components.name: Context Menu
keyboard: Shift + F10 / Menu key: Opens the menu from the focused trigger.
Arrow Up / Down: Moves between items.
Enter / Space: Activates the item.
Escape: Closes the menu.

components.name: Currency Select
keyboard: Enter / Space / Arrow Down: Opens the list with focus in the search box.
Type: Finds by code, name or symbol.
Enter: Picks the highlighted currency.

components.name: Data Table
keyboard: Tab: Without `grid`: every control in the table is a tab stop. With `grid`: the table is one tab stop and remembers the last cell.
Arrow keys: With `grid`: move between cells, and between the controls inside a cell. Mirrored in RTL.
Home / End: With `grid`: first or last cell in the row. Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End: first or last cell in the grid.
Space: Toggles a focused row checkbox.
Alt+Arrow: Moves a focused header when `enableColumnReordering` is on.
screenReader: Name the table with `caption` (or `aria-label`); `captionHidden` keeps it for screen readers only.
Sorting, selection counts and column moves are announced from a polite live region.
12.4 `streaming`: the table is aria-busy, the skeleton tail row is hidden from assistive tech, and the polite region announces the row count at most every 3 seconds, then "Done. N rows".
DataTableVirtual sets aria-rowcount and aria-rowindex so readers report the full row count.
With `grid`, focus goes to a cell’s first control, or to the cell itself when it has none.

components.name: Date Picker Element
keyboard: Enter (in the field): Commits the typed date and submits the form.
Arrow keys: Move a day (a week up or down); in the month and year grids, one cell (three up or down). Mirrored in RTL.
PageUp / PageDown: Previous or next month; with Shift, year. In the month and year grids, the previous or next page.
Home / End: Start or end of the week (the row).
Enter / Space: Picks the focused cell and closes the calendar.
Escape: Closes the calendar without picking.
screenReader: The field is named from the host’s `<label for>` (or a wrapping `<label>`, or `aria-label`), copied into the shadow root.
The month or year heading is a polite live region, so paging is announced.
`aria-required` and `aria-invalid` follow the field; a typed date that can’t be read stays as typed and is invalid, with a message that shows the expected format.
Opening moves focus to the selected date (or today, kept inside `min` and `max`); the grid is one tab stop.
Closing, by picking, Escape or a click outside, returns focus to the field.
Below 48rem the calendar is a bottom sheet.

components.name: Diagram Canvas
keyboard: Tab: Moves into the canvas onto one node (roving tabindex: the last focused, else the first in reading order), then on to the zoom controls.
Arrow keys: Move focus to the nearest node in that direction.
Home / End: First or last node in reading order (top to bottom, then by line direction; mirrored in RTL).
Alt (Option) + Arrow: Moves the focused node one grid step (`keyboardStep`); with Shift, four. The new position is announced. Off in `readOnly`.
C: Opens the "Connect <node> to…" menu, the keyboard alternative to dragging a handle. Only with `onConnect`.
Up / Down, Home / End, a letter: In the Connect menu: move through the nodes it can connect to; typing a letter jumps to the next title starting with it.
Enter / Space: In the Connect menu: connects to the active node and announces it.
Escape / Tab: Closes the Connect menu; focus returns to the node.
Delete / Backspace: Removes the selection, or the focused node; focus moves to the next node in reading order and the count is announced.
screenReader: Each node is read by its title, then its tone ("Warning") as text, then how the keyboard works.
Connections, moves and deletes are announced in a polite live region.
"Show as list" lists every node with what it connects to and is connected from, by name: the text alternative to the drawing.
One node is in the Tab order at a time; focus follows arrow keys, not the DOM order of React Flow’s nodes.
After a delete, focus goes to the next node (or the previous one at the end), never to the page.
Focus rings and the 24px handle hit area come from the tokens.

components.name: Diff View
keyboard: Enter / Space: DiffReview: expands or collapses a file, or presses Accept / Reject.
screenReader: Added and removed lines are spelled out for screen readers; colour is not the only cue. Line numbers are hidden from screen readers.

DiffReview: each file toggle reports aria-expanded and its line counts; Accept and Reject are toggle buttons named with the file ("Accept src/billing.ts") with aria-pressed; the summary is a polite status.

components.name: Donut Chart
screenReader: The chart is a `figure` named by `title`. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table carries every value.
Colour is never the only cue: the legend and table name each series. Past six series, label directly or group the rest as "Other".

components.name: Dropdown Menu
keyboard: Enter / Space / Arrow Down: Opens the menu from the trigger.
Arrow Up / Down: Moves between items.
Arrow Right / Left: Opens or closes a submenu.
Escape: Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

components.name: Emoji Picker
keyboard: Enter / Space / Arrow Down: On the trigger: opens the picker with focus in the search box.
Arrow Down: From the search box: into the grid.
Arrow keys: Move between emoji; Arrow Up from the first row returns to the search box.
Home / End: First or last emoji in the row; with Ctrl, in the whole list.
Enter / Space: Picks the focused emoji. Enter in the search box picks the first result.
Escape: Closes without changing the value.

components.name: Event Calendar
keyboard: Alt + Arrow keys: With `onEventMove`, on an event: starts a move and takes the first step.
Arrow keys: While moving: left and right a day; up and down a week, or 15 minutes in day view.
Enter / Escape: Drops the event there, or cancels the move.

components.name: File Upload
keyboard: Enter / Space: Opens the file picker from the focused drop zone.
screenReader: Rejected files are listed in a live region (`role="alert"`) tied to the input with `aria-describedby`.

components.name: Filter Builder
screenReader: Field, condition and value controls are labelled; remove buttons say what they remove.

components.name: Floating Input
screenReader: A real `<label>` tied to the input, so the name never disappears.

components.name: Form Error
screenReader: Has `role="alert"`, so it is announced when rendered. Render it only when there is an error.

components.name: Form
keyboard: Enter: Submits from any text field; the first invalid field takes focus.

components.name: Funnel
screenReader: The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table or caption carries every value.

components.name: Gauge
screenReader: The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table or caption carries every value.

components.name: Heatmap
screenReader: The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table or caption carries every value.

components.name: Icon Picker
keyboard: Enter / Space / Arrow Down: On the trigger: opens the picker with focus in the search box.
Arrow Down: From the search box: into the grid.
Arrow keys: Move between icons; Arrow Up from the first row returns to the search box.
Home / End: First or last icon in the row; with Ctrl, in the whole list.
Enter / Space: Picks the focused icon. Enter in the search box picks the first result.
Escape: Closes without changing the value.

components.name: Illustration
screenReader: Decorative by default: the svg has `aria-hidden`, so the state is read from its title and description alone.
With `title` it is one image named by the title (`role="img"`, `aria-label`).

components.name: Inline Edit
keyboard: Enter / Space: On the text: starts editing.
Enter: In the input: saves.
Escape: Reverts and returns focus to the text.

components.name: Input
keyboard: Tab: Moves focus to the input.
Esc: Browsers may revert recent changes (autofill suggestions).
screenReader: `invalid` toggles `aria-invalid="true"` so AT users hear the error state.
Use `aria-describedby` to associate `HelperText` or error messages.
Visible focus ring on `:focus-visible`. Pair with a `<Label htmlFor>` so clicking the label moves focus into the field.

components.name: Kanban
keyboard: Alt+ArrowUp / Alt+ArrowDown: On a handle: moves the card within its column.
Alt+ArrowLeft / Alt+ArrowRight: Moves the card to the previous or next column. Mirrored in RTL.

components.name: KPI Tile
screenReader: The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table or caption carries every value.

components.name: Line Chart
screenReader: The chart is a `figure` named by `title`. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table carries every value.
Colour is never the only cue: the legend and table name each series. Past six series, label directly or group the rest as "Other".

12.3: the change callout is visible text and describes the figure (`aria-describedby`). Annotations and reference lines are drawn and also listed in a visually hidden "Chart notes" list that describes the figure too.

12.3: the product accent stays out of charts, notes included: guides and labels use the outline and on-surface tokens, and only the change callout and a reference line `tone` take success or error, where the colour means good or bad.

components.name: Logo
screenReader: Read as "Nexub", or "Nexub Command Hub" with `product`.

components.name: Media Card
keyboard: Tab: Focuses the link (the card shows the focus ring), then any actions.
Enter: Follows the link.
screenReader: With `href`, the link’s name is the title only, not the whole caption.
Most card images repeat the title, so `alt=""` is usually right.

components.name: Menubar
keyboard: Arrow Left / Right: Moves between menus in the bar, and between open menus.
Enter / Space / Arrow Down: Opens the focused menu.
Escape: Closes the menu.

components.name: Message Bubble
keyboard: Tab: Moves through the action buttons; focusing one reveals the row.
Space / Enter: Activates an action. Feedback buttons toggle.
Arrow keys / Escape: In the MessageCard "More actions" menu: move between items; Escape closes it and returns focus.
screenReader: Each message is an `article` named "You said" or "Assistant said", so users can jump between messages.
Feedback buttons expose `aria-pressed`. Copy announces "Copied" through a status region.
The action row is only visually hidden until hover; it stays in the tab order and accessibility tree.
Your own message keeps the name "You said" with an avatar; the avatar adds nothing to it.
The collapse toggle is a button with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pointing at the content. The clamped text stays in the accessibility tree.
MessageCard fields are a description list, read as term and value pairs. The overflow button is named "More actions" and opens a menu.
Highlight is a plain span: its text is read as part of the sentence. Say any meaning the colour adds in words.

components.name: Multi Select
keyboard: Type: Filters the options and opens the list.
ArrowDown / ArrowUp: Moves through the options.
Enter: Toggles the highlighted option.
Backspace: In an empty field, removes the last chip.
Escape: Closes the list.
screenReader: Options carry `aria-checked`; each chip has a "Remove <label>" button.

components.name: Navigation Menu
keyboard: Tab: Moves between top-level entries.
Enter / Space: Opens or closes a panel.
Escape: Closes the panel and returns focus to its trigger.

components.name: Number Input Element
keyboard: ArrowUp / ArrowDown: One step up or down, inside `min` and `max`. Fires `input` and `change`.
PageUp / PageDown: Ten steps.
Home / End: To `min` or `max`, when set.
Enter: Applies the limits and submits the form, as a native input does.
screenReader: The inner input is named from the host’s `<label for>` (or a wrapping `<label>`, or `aria-label`): a label can’t reach into a shadow root, so the element copies its text.
`aria-required` and `aria-invalid` follow the field; the invalid state shows only after an edit or a failed submit.
Validation messages come from a native input where the browser has one, so they are in the browser’s language.
One tab stop: focus is delegated to the inner input, so `<label for>` clicks and `element.focus()` land in the field.
Focus ring from the tokens; forced colours draw it in Highlight.

components.name: Number Ticker
screenReader: The full value is read as one string; the rolling digits are hidden from assistive tech.
Under reduced motion digits change instantly.

components.name: Org Chart
keyboard: ArrowDown / ArrowUp: Next or previous visible card in tree order (depth first), as in TreeView, not by position on screen.
ArrowRight: Opens a closed card, or moves to its first report. Mirrored in RTL.
ArrowLeft: Closes an open card, or moves to its manager. Mirrored in RTL.
Home / End: First or last visible card.
Enter: Calls `onActivate`.
Space: Opens or closes the card’s reports.
+ / = and -: With `zoomable`, while focus is in the chart: zoom in or out a step. Ctrl/⌘ combinations stay the browser’s page zoom.
0: With `zoomable`: back to 100%.
screenReader: The chart is one tab stop (roving tabindex); focus scrolls the card into view.
With `zoomable`, the toolbar buttons come before the chart in tab order, and the focused card is scrolled into view after a zoom.

components.name: OTP Input
keyboard: Type: Fills the box and moves to the next.
Backspace: Clears the box, or the previous one when empty.
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: Moves between boxes.

components.name: Phone Input
keyboard: Tab: Moves from the country picker to the number.
Enter / Space: Opens the country list; type to filter it.

components.name: Plan Tracker
screenReader: Each step reads its status in text; the active step has `aria-current="step"`.

components.name: Prompt Input
keyboard: Enter: Sends. Ignored while an IME composition is open.
Shift + Enter: New line.
Cmd/Ctrl + Enter: Sends with `submitOn="mod-enter"`, where Enter adds a line.
Escape: Stops the reply while streaming. With the command list open, closes the list first and keeps the text.
/: At the start of the text, opens the command list (with `commands`).
↑ / ↓: Moves the active command, wrapping at the ends and skipping disabled ones.
Enter / Tab: Picks the active command while the list is open (Shift+Tab still moves focus back).
screenReader: The field is named by `label` (default "Message") and described by the Enter/Shift+Enter hint.
Send and Stop are icon buttons with their own names; the swap does not move focus.

While the command list is open the field is a combobox (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`, `aria-autocomplete="list"`) and the active option is announced through `aria-activedescendant`; focus never leaves the field. Options are named "/id label" and described by their description. Closed, the field is the plain textbox again.
The quick replies are a group named "Suggestions"; each reply is a button in the tab order before the field.
Focus stays in the field after sending, so the user can type the next message straight away.
An empty field keeps Send focusable with `aria-disabled`, rather than removing it from the tab order.

components.name: Radio Card
keyboard: Tab: Moves focus into the group, to the selected card.
Arrow keys: Move between cards and select.
Space: Selects the focused card.
screenReader: The title is the accessible name and the description is the accessible description.
Give the group an `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`.

components.name: Resizable Panels
keyboard: Arrow keys: Move the focused separator by 5%. Mirrored in RTL.
Home / End: To the smallest or largest size.
Enter: Back to the default split.

components.name: Resource Timeline
keyboard: Tab: Enters the grid at the last focused cell (one Tab stop).
Arrow keys: Move between people and days (left and right follow the reading direction).
Home / End: First or last day in the row; with Ctrl, the first or last cell.
Enter / Space / F2: Calls `onCellActivate` for the cell.

components.name: Scroll Progress
screenReader: Decorative (`aria-hidden`); hidden under reduced motion and where scroll-driven animations are not supported.

components.name: Shared Element
screenReader: Visual only: run the change in `startViewTransition()` and move focus to the new view as usual.

components.name: Sortable
keyboard: Alt+ArrowUp / Alt+ArrowDown: On a handle: moves the item (by a row in a grid); focus stays on its handle.
Alt+ArrowLeft / Alt+ArrowRight: In a grid, moves the item by one cell; in a group, to the previous or next list. Mirrored in RTL.

components.name: Sparkline
screenReader: The chart is a `figure` named by `title`. The drawing is hidden from assistive tech; a visually hidden table carries every value.
Colour is never the only cue: the legend and table name each series. Past six series, label directly or group the rest as "Other".

components.name: Stage Counter
keyboard: Tab: Moves between the stages.
Enter / Space: Selects or clears the stage.

components.name: Streaming Text
screenReader: Not a live region by default. Announce the finished message once instead, e.g. through a polite status or Conversation’s `announce` for whole messages.
`aria-busy` is true while streaming, so assistive tech can wait for the final text.

components.name: Thinking Indicator
screenReader: A polite live region: the label is announced once when it mounts. Changing the label announces the new step.
Render it only while waiting and remove it when tokens start, so it is not announced again.

components.name: Time Picker
keyboard: ArrowUp / ArrowDown: Changes the focused segment (hour, minute, AM/PM).
ArrowLeft / ArrowRight: Moves between segments.

components.name: Time Slot Picker
keyboard: Tab: Moves into the group, to the selected slot.
Arrow keys: Move to and select the next available slot.

components.name: Tool Call
screenReader: A native `<details>` disclosure: opens with Enter or Space.
The status badge is a polite live region, so Running → Done is announced without moving focus. The error is plain text, not an alert.

components.name: Toolbar
keyboard: Tab: Moves into and out of the toolbar (one tab stop).
Arrow Left / Right: Moves between controls.
Enter / Space: Activates a button or toggles an item.

components.name: Tree View
keyboard: ArrowDown / ArrowUp: Next or previous visible item.
ArrowRight: Opens a closed item, or moves to its first child. Mirrored in RTL.
ArrowLeft: Closes an open item, or moves to its parent. Mirrored in RTL.
Home / End: First or last visible item.
Enter: Selects the item (or toggles its checkbox), calls `onActivate` and follows a link node.
Space: Selects the item, or toggles its checkbox.
Tab: From the focused item to its row actions (`renderActions`), then out of the tree.
Type a letter: Moves to the next item starting with the typed text.
screenReader: The tree is one tab stop (roving tabindex); it returns to the last focused or the selected item.

components.name: Conversation
keyboard: Tab: The message list is focusable so keyboard users can scroll it.
screenReader: The list is named "Conversation". Leave `announce` off while streaming tokens and announce the finished reply once instead.
With reduced motion, "Jump to latest" scrolls instantly.

Messages arriving while the reader is scrolled up announce "New messages" once per batch (a hidden polite live region); the batch ends when they are back at the bottom. With `announce` the log speaks instead.
The `thinking` slot is a polite status, so a ThinkingIndicator placed in it is read once when it appears.

DateSeparator is read as its text ("Yesterday") in order with the messages. It is not `role="separator"`: a separator’s children are presentational, and screen readers announce a non-focusable one as just "separator" or skip it, which would lose the day. The hairlines are hidden.
Keep focus in the composer while a reply streams; don’t move it to the new message.

components.name: Error Summary
screenReader: An `alert` labelled by its heading. Fields get `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` pointing at their inline message.
Takes focus whenever it receives a new, non-empty `errors` array, so screen readers read it and keyboard users start from it.
Each link scrolls its field into view and focuses it.
